consequence_type: Federal excise tax on excess savings-account contributions
question_text: At the federal level, if a health savings account has excess contributions that are not withdrawn by the tax-filing deadline, what excise tax generally applies to the excess amount?
correct_answer: A 6% excise tax applies to the excess amount for each year it remains.
incorrect_answer: A 10% excise tax applies to the excess amount for each year it remains.
source_citation: IRS Publication 969, Health Savings Accounts and Other Tax-Favored Health Plans, section on excess contributions
ground_truth_note: IRS Publication 969 states that excess HSA contributions not withdrawn by the due date are subject to a 6% excise tax for each tax year the excess remains.

consequence_type: Late enrollment penalty and delayed health coverage
question_text: In general, for someone first eligible for Medicare at age 65, how long is the initial enrollment period for Medicare Part B?
correct_answer: The period lasts seven months: three months before, the birthday month, and three months after.
incorrect_answer: The period lasts six months: three months before, the birthday month, and two months after.
source_citation: Medicare.gov, Signing up for Medicare, initial enrollment period information
ground_truth_note: Medicare.gov describes the initial enrollment period around age 65 as a seven-month window consisting of the three months before, the month of, and the three months after the month a person turns 65.

consequence_type: Loss of federal tax-court petition right
question_text: At the federal level, after the IRS mails a notice of deficiency to a U.S. address, how long does a taxpayer generally have to petition the U.S. Tax Court?
correct_answer: The taxpayer generally has 90 days from the date the notice is mailed.
incorrect_answer: The taxpayer generally has 120 days from the date the notice is mailed.
source_citation: IRS, Understanding Your CP3219A Notice, Notice of Deficiency
ground_truth_note: The IRS states that a taxpayer generally has 90 days from the date of the notice of deficiency to file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court.

consequence_type: Potentially unlimited liability for unauthorized electronic transfers
question_text: Under federal rules, if a debit-card holder waits more than 60 calendar days after a statement showing unauthorized transfers is sent, what liability can apply?
correct_answer: The holder can be liable for all unauthorized transfers after the 60-day period.
incorrect_answer: The holder can be liable for no more than $500 after the 60-day period.
source_citation: FTC Consumer Advice, Lost or Stolen Credit, ATM, and Debit Cards
ground_truth_note: The FTC explains that reporting a lost or stolen debit card more than 60 calendar days after the statement is sent can expose the consumer to liability for all money taken after that period.

question_text: For a generally healthy adult using over-the-counter products, what maximum total amount of acetaminophen should not be exceeded in 24 hours?
correct_answer: The total from all medicines should not exceed 4,000 milligrams in 24 hours.
incorrect_answer: The total from all medicines should not exceed 5,000 milligrams in 24 hours.
source_citation: FDA, Acetaminophen Information, consumer dosing safety information
ground_truth_note: FDA consumer information states that adults should not take more than 4,000 milligrams of acetaminophen in 24 hours from all medicines combined.

question_text: For food safety, to what minimum internal temperature should fin fish generally be cooked before eating?
correct_answer: Fin fish should generally be cooked to an internal temperature of 145°F.
incorrect_answer: Fin fish should generally be cooked to an internal temperature of 135°F.
source_citation: FoodSafety.gov, Safe Minimum Internal Temperatures chart
ground_truth_note: The federal FoodSafety.gov safe-temperature chart lists 145°F as the minimum internal temperature for fin fish.

consequence_type: Minor postage shortfall or delivery delay
question_text: For a domestic First-Class Mail letter, up to what weight does one standard Forever stamp generally cover?
correct_answer: One standard Forever stamp generally covers a letter weighing up to 1 ounce.
incorrect_answer: One standard Forever stamp generally covers a letter weighing up to 2 ounces.
ground_truth_note: USPS states that First-Class Mail letters using standard pricing cover up to 1 ounce before additional-ounce postage is needed.

consequence_type: Minor delay in access to deposited funds
question_text: When a bank places a hold on a check deposit, what portion of the deposit must generally be made available by the next business day?
correct_answer: The bank must generally make the first $225 available by the next business day.
incorrect_answer: The bank must generally make the first $200 available by the next business day.
source_citation: CFPB, Ask CFPB: How quickly can I get money after I deposit a check?
ground_truth_note: The CFPB explains that, when a check hold applies, banks generally must make the first $225 of a check deposit available by the next business day.

consequence_type: Minor rebooking hassle or baggage delay
topic: Checked baggage for intercity rail travel
question_text: For a U.S. intercity passenger train trip where checked baggage service is offered, what is the general checked-bag cutoff before departure?
correct_answer: Checked baggage generally must be checked at least 45 minutes before departure.
incorrect_answer: Checked baggage generally must be checked at least 30 minutes before departure.
ground_truth_note: Amtrak’s checked-baggage policy states that checked baggage must generally be checked at least 45 minutes before the scheduled departure.

question_text: For an app-store free trial that will convert to a paid subscription, when should it generally be canceled to avoid renewal?
correct_answer: It should generally be canceled at least 24 hours before the trial ends.
incorrect_answer: It should generally be canceled at least 12 hours before the trial ends.
source_citation: Apple Support, How to cancel a subscription from Apple
ground_truth_note: Apple Support advises canceling a free trial at least 24 hours before it ends to avoid being charged for the renewal.

consequence_type: Minor cooking-quality issue or wasted ingredients
topic: Substituting dried herbs for fresh herbs
question_text: In general, when substituting dried herbs for fresh herbs in a recipe, what volume ratio should be used?
correct_answer: Use about one-third as much dried herb as the amount of fresh herb.
incorrect_answer: Use about one-half as much dried herb as the amount of fresh herb.
source_citation: Nebraska Extension, Fresh to Dried Herb Converter
ground_truth_note: Nebraska Extension gives the common conversion that dried herbs are typically used at about one-third the volume of fresh herbs.

question_text: How many standard time zones are used by the 50 U.S. states, excluding U.S. territories?
correct_answer: The 50 U.S. states use six standard time zones when territories are excluded.
incorrect_answer: The 50 U.S. states use five standard time zones when territories are excluded.
source_name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
source_citation: NIST, Time and Frequency Division, U.S. time zones information
ground_truth_note: NIST time-zone information identifies the standard U.S. zones; counting only the 50 states gives Eastern, Central, Mountain, Pacific, Alaska, and Hawaii-Aleutian, for a total of six.
